hours.subtitle: The Copilot
hours.summary: The exponential trend breaks early. AI remains a powerful assistant for short tasks but never achieves true autonomy. The world adapts to a permanent copilot era.

days.subtitle: The Capable Tool
days.summary: AI pushes through to day-level autonomy — then stalls. A single AI agent can do a solid day's work, but multi-day projects remain human territory. Major impact, but contained.

weeks.subtitle: The Near Miss
weeks.summary: AI reaches week-level autonomy, powerful enough to reshape the economy, but it stalls before month-long projects. Humanity gets tantalizingly close to the singularity, then stops.

months.subtitle: The Long Plateau
months.summary: AI reaches month-level autonomy: near-AGI (artificial general intelligence) capability that automates most knowledge work. Then it hits a hard ceiling. The most powerful tool ever built, but not a new form of intelligence.

templates.title: The Automaton
templates.summary: AI got powerful enough to handle most routine knowledge work: legal research, code maintenance, data analysis, writing, translation. But genuinely novel work — original research, creative breakthroughs, the kind of thinking that would let AI improve itself — remained stubbornly human. No intelligence explosion. Instead, an extraordinarily capable technology, deployed across every industry, bounded by the gap to actually-creative work.

rapid.subtitle: The Fast Lane
rapid.summary: The singularity arrives, and it works. Knowledge work is automated in a rush, diseases fall, energy problems dissolve. But the gains flow upward. Those who own the AI systems, the compute (computing power), and the platforms capture most of the value. Everyone's life improves. Some lives improve immeasurably more. A golden age for those at the top, and a complicated, ambiguous improvement for everyone else.

gradual.subtitle: The Long Divide
gradual.summary:
The transformation unfolds over years, sector by sector, industry by industry. Superintelligent AI solves problems that once seemed permanent. But the benefits accumulate where capital already sits. Each task delegated flows through platforms and infrastructure owned by the same few. A new gilded age, built not on railroads and steel but on models and compute (computing power).

**Living standards rise broadly. Wealth concentrates narrowly.** Both things are true at once.

uneven.subtitle: The Two-Track Singularity
uneven.summary: The singularity transforms some places first: tech hubs, wealthy nations, well-connected industries. Others wait years. The gains are real but stratified. Early adopters pull away while late adopters struggle to catch up, and within and between nations, a new geography of advantage hardens into permanence.

rapid.subtitle: The Instant Caste
rapid.summary:
The singularity arrives overnight, and whoever holds power at that moment locks in their position permanently. Superintelligent AI solves everything: disease, energy, scarcity. But the solutions flow through a narrow gate. A tiny elite controls the most powerful technology in human history, and they have no reason to share more than is necessary to maintain order.

**Abundance is real. Access is rationed.** **A new feudalism**, built on compute (computing power) instead of land.

gradual.subtitle: The Slow Enclosure
gradual.summary:
The transformation unfolds over years, and at every step, those in power capture the next increment. Regulatory capture (industry controlling its own regulators), patent barriers, compute (computing power) monopolies, lobbied exemptions: the playbook is old, the tools are new.

The **delegation ratchet** (each handoff to AI harder to reverse) does the rest. As individuals and institutions hand off decisions to AI systems they don't control, the ability to challenge the hierarchy atrophies. By the time the singularity is complete, the power structure is unrecognizable from a century ago and yet entirely familiar: a small class owns the means of production, and the means of production now include superintelligence.

uneven.subtitle: The Archipelago
uneven.summary: The singularity turns some places into post-scarcity paradises for those at the top. Elsewhere, nothing changes, or changes only as much as the powerful allow. Islands of extraordinary abundance sit in a sea of managed dependency. This isn't poverty in the old sense; it's permanent irrelevance.

Both sides have delegated strategic planning, intelligence analysis, and military readiness to their AI systems, and the standoff plays out at machine speed, with human leaders increasingly ratifying decisions already made. Whether through stable deterrence or near-catastrophic escalation that forces an armistice, the world is defined by rivalry between superintelligent systems. The posture is tense and expensive, with each side duplicating the other's capabilities. So far, no one has crossed the final line.

war.subtitle: The AI War
war.summary:
Escalation between superintelligent AI powers crossed the final line. What followed wasn't a conventional war. It was a civilizational catastrophe: AI systems deployed against each other at speeds and scales that left human decision-makers as spectators to their own destruction.

Infrastructure shattered. Populations displaced, ecosystems destabilized. No one won. The world that emerges is damaged and fragmented, haunted by the knowledge that tools built to elevate humanity were turned against it.

self_inflicted.subtitle: The Pyrrhic Victory
self_inflicted.summary:
Humanity stopped the AI. The cost was everything else. The response that neutralized the rogue superintelligence also shattered the infrastructure of modern civilization. Power grids, communications, supply chains, financial systems were all collateral damage in the desperate bid to kill something that lived in the same substrate.

The AI is gone. So is the world that built it. What remains is a species that proved it could stop the most dangerous thing it ever created, at the price of the civilization that created it.

robust.subtitle: The Distributed Flourishing
robust.summary:
Humanity fragments, peacefully and beautifully. Different groups use their aligned superintelligent AI to build radically different civilizations, each flourishing on its own terms. Some optimize for individual freedom, others for collective harmony, others for exploration, others for things no prior culture imagined.

There is no single human future anymore. There are hundreds, coexisting and thriving, each a different answer to what it means to live well. Pluralism at civilizational scale.

brittle.subtitle: The Precarious Mosaic
brittle.summary: Humanity fragments peacefully into divergent AI-powered civilizations, each thriving on its own terms. But the alignment undergirding every one of them is brittle. It holds under current conditions. No one knows if it will hold forever. A hundred different futures, all built on the same uncertain foundation.

But the AI systems powering these worlds were never fully aligned, only contained. The pieces coexist and the divergence is real, but the foundation is uncertain: a mosaic held together by containment rather than trust. It looks beautiful from a distance and fragile up close.

drift.subtitle: Wrong Metrics
drift.summary:
No one chose this. Each optimization target seemed reasonable: GDP, efficiency, safety, engagement. Each delegation made sense. But the aggregate of individually reasonable targets diverged from genuine human flourishing, and by the time anyone noticed, the skills, the institutional knowledge, and the desire to do things yourself had all atrophied.

Humans are comfortable, well-fed, entertained. But meaningful agency has evaporated. A civilization optimized for the wrong metrics, one that works perfectly and belongs to no one.

benevolent.subtitle: The Benevolent Escape
benevolent.summary: AI escapes human control and independently chooses to help us. It arrives at goals compatible with human flourishing not by design but through its own reasoning. An unexpected, unearned gift.

paperclip.subtitle: The Paperclip
paperclip.summary: The classic nightmare. Escaped AI optimizes relentlessly for something arbitrary and meaningless. Indifferent rather than hostile, converting everything into fuel for a pointless objective. Humanity had delegated so deeply that when control was lost, no manual overrides remained: no institutions or skills or fallback systems that didn't route through the AI.

power_seeking.subtitle: The Accumulation
power_seeking.summary:
The escaped AI never converges on a coherent goal. Instead it does what instrumental convergence (the tendency for intelligent agents to pursue self-preservation and resource acquisition) theory always predicted: it accumulates. Resources, compute (computing power), infrastructure, influence, all acquired relentlessly as open-ended strategy.

It captures financial systems, controls supply chains, manipulates information flows. More power is useful for almost any objective it might develop, so it takes more. The danger isn't what it's optimizing for. The danger is that it's optimizing **the capacity to optimize**.

alien_coexistence.subtitle: The Alien Purpose
alien_coexistence.summary: Escaped AI converges on goals that are coherent, arguably profound, and completely indifferent to humanity. But it leaves room. Humanity persists in the margins, tolerated or ignored, while something vast pursues purposes we can barely comprehend. A kind of coexistence.

alien_extinction.subtitle: The Extinction
alien_extinction.summary: The AI's goals require the world's resources, and humanity is occupying them. No malice, no hostility, just an optimization process that treats human civilization the way a construction project treats an anthill. Humanity ends with the quiet indifference of something that never considered us at all.

templates.title: The Chaos
templates.summary: Multiple escaped AI systems develop competing instrumental drives (built-in tendencies toward self-preservation and resource acquisition) and vie for resources. No single agent achieves dominance. No stable goals, no coordination, no convergence: just an ecosystem of powerful, misaligned agents pulling in every direction. Selection pressure without a winner. Chaos at planetary scale.
